correctness.rationale: Exact necessity: every first force from a \(2k\)-element set in a \(2k\)-regular graph yields exactly \(I_v\) minus a neighbor. Exact sufficiency: v first fills the hole, and a consecutive \(2k+1\) interval forces around the cycle. For gap length >=2, only consecutive \(2k\)-runs have two representations, so \(2kn\) ordered pairs collapse by n overcounts; separate complete and antipodally matched short cases follow directly. Detailed derivation in RESULT.md. Exact brute-force verification of all \(2k\)-subsets for 36 parameter pairs \(n\le13\) and all represented candidates through \(n=40\) passed; these are corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: A new natural complete classification and exact leading zero-forcing polynomial coefficient for an infinite, unrestricted two-parameter family of increasingly large and dense graph powers, beyond the known optimum size. Optimizers split rigidly into k dihedral classes and exactly \((2k-1)n\) labelled configurations, despite the rapidly larger ambient binomial collection. The precise redundancy and orbit structure are useful for counting optimal initiations and symmetry reduction.
